LESSON: MASS, VOLUME, WEIGHT AND DENSITY

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: MEASU REMEN TS
Topic 3.3: Mass, Volume, Weight and Density
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Mass, Volume, Weight and Density, part of MEASU REMEN TS in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 9 MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: How do you weigh materials and objects? 2. How do we use density in daily life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Mass, Volume, Weight and Density together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: The learner speaks engagingly by using facts and examples to support points when

they are discussing the relationship between mass and weight.

● Learning to learn: The learner organises their own learning as they collect and weigh different materials or objects and

change one unit of mass to another.

30

Values:
● Integrity: The learner enhances discipline as they give correct mass and weights of different material and objects.

● Responsibility: The learner enhances diligence as they work and take care of weighing machines and other resources.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Self-awareness: The learner weighs themselves for health purposes.

Link to other subjects:

● Agriculture and Nutrition: The learner weighs different quantities for a variety of recipes.

● Integrated Science: The learner uses machines and tools which involve weighing and balancing.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Digital devices with assistive technology such as screen readers, screen magnifiers and adapted keyboard, objects/containers,

weighing scales, Print and Braille Course Book.
